label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs))
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (AP التفاضل والتكامل AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs))

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

الشرح الرياضي (الأسئلة المقالية الحرة (FRQs) في اختبار AP Calculus AB):

Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example A — AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول A — AP التفاضل والتكامل AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): A differentiable function \( f \) is defined on the interval \( [-4, 4] \). The graph of \( f' \), the derivative of \( f \), is shown in the figure above. The graph of \( f' \) consists of two line segments and a semicircle. (a) Find the value of \( f(2) - f(-2) \). Show the setup for your answer. (b) For how many values of \( c \) in the interval \( (-4, 4) \) does \( f'(c) = 0 \)? Explain your reasoning. (c) The function \( f \) has a local maximum at \( x = k \). Find the value of \( k \). Explain your reasoning. (d) The function \( f \) has an inflection point at \( x = p \). Find the value of \( p \). Explain your reasoning.

Step-by-Step Solution: **(a)** By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, \( f(2) - f(-2) = \int_{-2}^{2} f'(x) \, dx \). The region from \( x = -2 \) to \( x = 2 \) is a semicircle with radius 2. The area of this semicircle is \( \frac{1}{2} \pi (2)^2 = 2\pi \). Therefore, \( f(2) - f(-2) = 2\pi \). **(b)** The graph of \( f'(x) \) is shown. \( f'(c) = 0 \) when the graph of \( f' \) intersects the x-axis. This occurs at \( x = -4 \) and \( x = 2 \). Since we are looking for values of \( c \) in the open interval \( (-4, 4) \), there is one such value, \( c = 2 \). **(c)** A local maximum of \( f \) occurs when \( f' \) changes from positive to negative. Looking at the graph of \( f' \), this occurs at \( x = 2 \), where \( f' \) changes from positive to negative. Therefore, \( k = 2 \). **(d)** An inflection point of \( f \) occurs when \( f'' \) changes sign. This means that \( f' \) changes from increasing to decreasing or vice versa. Looking at the graph of \( f' \), the slope of \( f' \) (which is \( f'' \)) changes at \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 2 \). At \( x = -2 \), \( f' \) changes from decreasing to increasing. At \( x = 2 \), \( f' \) changes from increasing to decreasing. Inflection points occur where the concavity of \( f \) changes, which is where \( f'' \) changes sign. The sign of \( f'' \) changes at \( x = -2 \) (from negative to positive) and at \( x = 2 \) (from positive to negative). However, the question asks for *an* inflection point. The graph of \( f' \) has a corner at \( x = -2 \), indicating a change in concavity of \( f \). The graph also has a point where the slope changes drastically at \( x=2 \) (from positive slope to zero slope for the semicircle). Looking closely at the graph, the derivative \( f' \) itself changes behavior at \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 2 \). The concavity of \( f \) changes where \( f'' \) changes sign. \( f'' \) is the slope of \( f' \). The slope of \( f' \) is negative for \( x < -2 \), zero for \( -2 < x < 2 \), and positive for \( x > 2 \). This means \( f'' \) changes sign at \( x = -2 \) (negative to zero, then zero to positive if we consider the end of the semicircle). The graph of \( f' \) has a corner at \( x = -2 \) and the slope of \( f' \) is 0 for \( x > 2 \). The concavity of \( f \) changes at \( x = -2 \). The rate of change of \( f' \) (which is \( f'' \)) changes from negative to positive at \( x=-2 \). Thus, \( p = -2 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): A differentiable الدالة \( f \) is defined on the interval \( [-4, 4] \). The التمثيل البياني of \( f' \), the المشتقة of \( f \), is shown in the الشكل above. The التمثيل البياني of \( f' \) consists of two line segments and a semicircle. (a) أوجد قيمة \( f(2) - f(-2) \). Show the setup for your الإجابة. (b) For how many values of \( c \) in the interval \( (-4, 4) \) does \( f'(c) = 0 \)? Explain your reasoning. (c) The الدالة \( f \) has a local maximum at \( x = k \). أوجد قيمة \( k \). Explain your reasoning. (d) The الدالة \( f \) has an نقطة الانعطاف at \( x = p \). أوجد قيمة \( p \). Explain your reasoning.

Step-by-Step الحل: **(a)** By the Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل, \( f(2) - f(-2) = \int_{-2}^{2} f'(x) \, dx \). The region from \( x = -2 \) to \( x = 2 \) is a semicircle with نصف القطر 2. The المساحة of this semicircle is \( \frac{1}{2} \pi (2)^2 = 2\pi \). وبالتالي, \( f(2) - f(-2) = 2\pi \). **(b)** The التمثيل البياني of \( f'(x) \) is shown. \( f'(c) = 0 \) عندما the التمثيل البياني of \( f' \) intersects the x-axis. This occurs at \( x = -4 \) and \( x = 2 \). Since we are looking for values of \( c \) in the open interval \( (-4, 4) \), there is one such value, \( c = 2 \). **(c)** A local maximum of \( f \) occurs عندما \( f' \) changes from positive to negative. Looking at the التمثيل البياني of \( f' \), this occurs at \( x = 2 \), حيث \( f' \) changes from positive to negative. وبالتالي, \( k = 2 \). **(d)** An نقطة الانعطاف of \( f \) occurs عندما \( f'' \) changes sign. This means that \( f' \) changes from increasing to decreasing or vice versa. Looking at the التمثيل البياني of \( f' \), the الميل of \( f' \) (which is \( f'' \)) changes at \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 2 \). At \( x = -2 \), \( f' \) changes from decreasing to increasing. At \( x = 2 \), \( f' \) changes from increasing to decreasing. Inflection points occur حيث the concavity of \( f \) changes, which is حيث \( f'' \) changes sign. The sign of \( f'' \) changes at \( x = -2 \) (from negative to positive) and at \( x = 2 \) (from positive to negative). However, the question asks for *an* نقطة الانعطاف. The التمثيل البياني of \( f' \) has a corner at \( x = -2 \), indicating a change in concavity of \( f \). The التمثيل البياني also has a point حيث the الميل changes drastically at \( x=2 \) (from positive الميل to zero الميل for the semicircle). Looking closely at the التمثيل البياني, the المشتقة \( f' \) itself changes behavior at \( x = -2 \) and \( x = 2 \). The concavity of \( f \) changes حيث \( f'' \) changes sign. \( f'' \) is the الميل of \( f' \). The الميل of \( f' \) is negative for \( x < -2 \), zero for \( -2 < x < 2 \), and positive for \( x > 2 \). This means \( f'' \) changes sign at \( x = -2 \) (negative to zero, then zero to positive if we consider the end of the semicircle). The التمثيل البياني of \( f' \) has a corner at \( x = -2 \) and the الميل of \( f' \) is 0 for \( x > 2 \). The concavity of \( f \) changes at \( x = -2 \). The rate of change of \( f' \) (which is \( f'' \)) changes from negative to positive at \( x=-2 \). وعليه, \( p = -2 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(B\) — AP التفاضل والتكامل AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Consider the function \( f(x) \) whose graph is shown below. The graph consists of a line segment and a quarter circle. The line segment connects the points \( (2, 4) \) and \( (4, 0) \). The quarter circle is in the second quadrant and is centered at \( (0, 0) \) with radius 2. Let \( A(x) \) be the area of the region bounded by the graph of \( f(t) \), the \( t \)-axis, and the lines \( t = 0 \) and \( t = x \). (a) Find \( A(3) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The function \( f(x) \) is defined piecewise. For \( 0 \le t \le 2 \), \( f(t) \) is the upper part of a circle centered at the origin with radius 2, so \( f(t) = \sqrt{4 - t^2} \). For \( 2 < t \le 4 \), \( f(t) \) is a line segment connecting \( (2, 4) \) and \( (4, 0) \). The equation of this line can be found using the two-point form: \( y - 0 = \frac{4 - 0}{2 - 4}(x - 4) \), which simplifies to \( y = -2(x - 4) \), so \( f(t) = -2(t - 4) \). To find \( A(3) \), we need to calculate the definite integral \( \int_{0}^{3} f(t) \, dt \). We split this integral into two parts based on the definition of \( f(t) \): \( A(3) = \int_{0}^{2} f(t) \, dt + \int_{2}^{3} f(t) \, dt \) For the first part, \( \int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{4 - t^2} \, dt \), this represents the area of a quarter circle of radius 2, which is \( \frac{1}{4}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{4}\pi (2^2) = \pi \). For the second part, \( \int_{2}^{3} (-2(t - 4)) \, dt \), we can evaluate this integral: \( \int_{2}^{3} (-2t + 8) \, dt = [-t^2 + 8t]_{2}^{3} \) Evaluating at the limits: \( (-3^2 + 8 \cdot 3) - (-2^2 + 8 \cdot 2) \) \( (-9 + 24) - (-4 + 16) \) \( 15 - 12 = 3 \). Therefore, \( A(3) = \pi + 3 \). *Common Misconceptions:* Students might incorrectly assume the function is a single simple shape or miscalculate the line segment's equation. They might also forget that the first part of the integral represents a quarter circle's area and attempt to integrate \( \sqrt{4-t^2} \) directly, which is more complex.
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): Consider the الدالة \( f(x) \) whose التمثيل البياني is shown below. The التمثيل البياني consists of a line segment and a quarter الدائرة. The line segment connects the points \( (2, 4) \) and \( (4, 0) \). The quarter الدائرة is in the second quadrant and is centered at \( (0, 0) \) with نصف القطر 2. Let \( A(x) \) be the المساحة of the region bounded by the التمثيل البياني of \( f(t) \), the \( t \)-axis, and the lines \( t = 0 \) and \( t = x \). (a) Find \( A(3) \).

Step-by-Step الحل: The الدالة \( f(x) \) is defined piecewise. For \( 0 \le t \le 2 \), \( f(t) \) is the upper part of a الدائرة centered at the origin with نصف القطر 2, so \( f(t) = \sqrt{4 - t^2} \). For \( 2 < t \le 4 \), \( f(t) \) is a line segment connecting \( (2, 4) \) and \( (4, 0) \). The المعادلة of this line can be found using the two-point form: \( y - 0 = \frac{4 - 0}{2 - 4}(x - 4) \), which simplifies to \( y = -2(x - 4) \), so \( f(t) = -2(t - 4) \). To find \( A(3) \), we need to احسب definite التكامل \( \int_{0}^{3} f(t) \, dt \). We split this التكامل into two parts based on the definition of \( f(t) \): \( A(3) = \int_{0}^{2} f(t) \, dt + \int_{2}^{3} f(t) \, dt \) For the first part, \( \int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{4 - t^2} \, dt \), this represents the المساحة of a quarter الدائرة of نصف القطر 2, which is \( \frac{1}{4}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{4}\pi (2^2) = \pi \). For the second part, \( \int_{2}^{3} (-2(t - 4)) \, dt \), we can احسب قيمة this التكامل: \( \int_{2}^{3} (-2t + 8) \, dt = [-t^2 + 8t]_{2}^{3} \) Evaluating at the النهايات: \( (-3^2 + 8 \cdot 3) - (-2^2 + 8 \cdot 2) \) \( (-9 + 24) - (-4 + 16) \) \( 15 - 12 = 3 \). وبالتالي, \( A(3) = \pi + 3 \). *Common Misconceptions:* Students might incorrectly assume the الدالة is a single simple shape or miscalculate the line segment's المعادلة. They might also forget that the first part of the التكامل represents a quarter الدائرة's المساحة and attempt to integrate \( \sqrt{4-t^2} \) directly, which is more complex.

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(C\) — AP التفاضل والتكامل AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): A particle's velocity is given by the function \(v(t) = 5\) for \(0 \le t \le 4\). Find the total displacement of the particle over this time interval.

Step-by-Step Solution: The displacement of the particle is the definite integral of its velocity function over the given time interval. \\ Displacement = \( \int_{0}^{4} v(t) \, dt = \int_{0}^{4} 5 \, dt \). \\ To evaluate this definite integral, we find the antiderivative of \(5\), which is \(5t\). \\ Then, we evaluate the antiderivative at the limits of integration: \\ \( [5t]_{0}^{4} = 5(4) - 5(0) = 20 - 0 = 20 \). \\ Therefore, the total displacement of the particle is 20 units.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): A particle's velocity is المعطيات by the الدالة \(v(t) = 5\) for \(0 \le t \le 4\). أوجد total displacement of the particle over this time interval.

Step-by-Step الحل: The displacement of the particle is the definite التكامل of its velocity الدالة over the المعطيات time interval. \\ Displacement = \( \int_{0}^{4} v(t) \, dt = \int_{0}^{4} 5 \, dt \). \\ To احسب قيمة this definite التكامل, we أوجد antiderivative of \(5\), which is \(5t\). \\ Then, we احسب قيمة antiderivative at the النهايات of integration: \\ \( [5t]_{0}^{4} = 5(4) - 5(0) = 20 - 0 = 20 \). \\ وبالتالي, the total displacement of the particle is 20 units.

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs) (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Let \( G(x) = \int_{18}^{x^{16}} \sqrt{t + 15} \, dt \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, what is \( G'(x) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Using FTC Part 1 and Chain Rule, \( G'(x) = \sqrt{x^{16} + 15} \cdot (16x^{15}) \).

label.en: ⚠️ Common Exam Traps — AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs)
label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة في الاختبار — AP التفاضل والتكامل AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs)

body.en:
1. Adding Successive Percentages or Averaging Speeds Arithmetically: On College Board AP Calculus AB, a \(20\%\) discount followed by a \(20\%\) increase gives \(0.80 \times 1.20 = 0.96\) (a net \(4\%\) loss, not \(0\%\)). Likewise, average speed for a round trip at \(40\) and \(60\text{ km/h}\) is \(\dfrac{2(40)(60)}{100} = 48\text{ km/h}\), never \(50\text{ km/h}\).

2. Failing to Flip the Inequality Sign When Multiplying/Dividing by a Negative: In \(-4x + 6 \le 10\), dividing by \(-4\) strictly reverses \(\le\) to \(\ge\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

On a Rate In / Rate Out FRQ, if rain falls into a cistern at rate \(R(t)\) and is pumped out at rate \(P(t)\), when is the amount of water in the cistern at a relative maximum?
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

On a Rate In / Rate Out FRQ, إذا كان rain falls into a cistern at rate \(R(t)\) and is pumped out at rate \(P(t)\), عندما is the amount of water in the cistern at a relative maximum?

solution.en: Let \(W(t)\) be the amount of water. \(W'(t) = R(t) - P(t)\). A relative maximum occurs when \(W'(t) = 0\) and changes from positive to negative, which occurs when \(R(t) = P(t)\) and \(R(t)\) crosses below \(P(t)\).

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

The graph of \(f'\) consists of a semicircle of radius 2 centered at the origin, lying above the x-axis. If \(f(0) = 5\), find the value of \(f(2)\).
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

The graph of \(f'\) consists of a semicircle of radius 2 centered at the origin, lying above the x-axis. إذا كان \(f(0) = 5\), أوجد قيمة \(f(2)\).

solution.en: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: \[ f(2) = f(0) + \int_0^2 f'(x)\,dx. \] The region under \(f'\) from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 2\) is a quarter-circle of radius 2: \[ \int_0^2 f'(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\pi(2^2) = \pi. \] Therefore, \[ f(2) = 5 + \pi \approx \mathbf{8.142}. \]
solution.ar: بتطبيق Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: \[ f(2) = f(0) + \int_0^2 f'(x)\,dx. \] The region under \(f'\) from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 2\) is a quarter-circle of radius 2: \[ \int_0^2 f'(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\pi(2^2) = \pi. \] وبالتالي، \[ f(2) = 5 + \pi \approx \mathbf{8.142}. \]

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

A differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = (y - 1)^2 \cos(x)\) has initial condition \(y(0) = 2\). Find the particular solution \(y = f(x)\).
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

A dإذا كانferential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = (y - 1)^2 \cos(x)\) has initial condition \(y(0) = 2\). أوجد الحل الخاص \(y = f(x)\).

solution.en: Separate variables: \[ \frac{dy}{(y-1)^2} = \cos(x)\,dx. \] Integrate both sides: \[ -\frac{1}{y - 1} = \sin(x) + C. \] Apply initial condition \(x = 0, y = 2\): \[ -\frac{1}{2 - 1} = \sin(0) + C \implies -1 = C. \] Substitute \(C = -1\): \[ -\frac{1}{y - 1} = \sin(x) - 1 \implies \frac{1}{y - 1} = 1 - \sin(x) \implies y - 1 = \frac{1}{1 - \sin(x)} \implies \mathbf{y = 1 + \frac{1}{1 - \sin(x)}}. \]
solution.ar: Separate variables: \[ \frac{dy}{(y-1)^2} = \cos(x)\,dx. \] Integrate both sides: \[ -\frac{1}{y - 1} = \sin(x) + C. \] Apply initial condition \(x = 0, y = 2\): \[ -\frac{1}{2 - 1} = \sin(0) + C \implies -1 = C. \] عوّض \(C = -1\): \[ -\frac{1}{y - 1} = \sin(x) - 1 \implies \frac{1}{y - 1} = 1 - \sin(x) \implies y - 1 = \frac{1}{1 - \sin(x)} \implies \mathbf{y = 1 + \frac{1}{1 - \sin(x)}}. \]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] Find the area of the region bounded by \( y = 11x \) and \( y = x^2 \) in the first quadrant.
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Hard] أوجد مساحة the region bounded by \( y = 11x \) and \( y = x^2 \) in the first quadrant.

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( x = 0 \) ، \( x = 11 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Set up the formula/expression: \(\text{Area} = \int_0^{11} (11x - x^2)\,dx\). Substitute and simplify: \(\text{Area} = \left[\frac{11}{2}x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{11}\).
hints.ar: جهّز الصيغة أو العبارة الرياضية: \(\text{Area} = \int_0^{11} (11x - x^2)\,dx\). عوّض بالقيم وبسّط العبارة: \(\text{Area} = \left[\frac{11}{2}x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{11}\).

solution.en: Intersections at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 11 \). Area \( = \int_0^{11} (11x - x^2)\,dx = \left[\frac{11}{2}x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{11} = \frac{1331}{6} \).

question.en: A particle moves along a straight line so that its velocity at time \( t \ge 0 \) is modeled by \( v(t) = 6t^2 - 18t + 12 \). At what time \( t \) is the acceleration of the particle equal to \( 0 \)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (AP Calculus AB Free-Response Questions (FRQs)): A particle moves along a straight line so that its velocity at time \( t \ge 0 \) is modeled by \( v(t) = 6t^2 - 18t + 12 \). At what time \( t \) is the acceleration of the particle equal to \( 0 \)?

hints.en: To find the acceleration \( a(t) \), take the derivative of the velocity function \( v(t) \) with respect to time \( t \): \(a(t) = v'(t) = \frac{d}{dt}(6t^2 - 18t + 12) = 12t - 18\).
hints.ar: To أوجد acceleration \( a(t) \), خذ المشتقة of the velocity function \( v(t) \) بالنسبة إلى time \( t \): \(a(t) = v'(t) = \frac{d}{dt}(6t^2 - 18t + 12) = 12t - 18\).

hints.en: Set \( a(t) = 0 \) and solve for \( t \): \(12t - 18 = 0\). Apply the next algebraic step: \(12t = 18\).
hints.ar: Set \( a(t) = 0 \) and أوجد قيمة \( t \): \(12t - 18 = 0\). طبّق الخطوة الجبرية التالية: \(12t = 18\).

solution.en:
To find the acceleration \( a(t) \), take the derivative of the velocity function \( v(t) \) with respect to time \( t \):
\[ a(t) = v'(t) = \frac{d}{dt}(6t^2 - 18t + 12) = 12t - 18. \]

Set \( a(t) = 0 \) and solve for \( t \):
\[ 12t - 18 = 0 \implies 12t = 18 \implies t = \frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}. \]

Common Misconceptions:
- Solving \( v(t) = 0 \) yields \( 6(t - 1)(t - 2) = 0 \implies t = 1 \) or \( t = 2 \). These are the times when the particle is at rest, not when its acceleration is zero.
- Omitting the factor of 2 when applying the power rule gives \( 6t - 18 = 0 \implies t = 3 \).
solution.ar:
To أوجد acceleration \( a(t) \), خذ المشتقة of the velocity function \( v(t) \) بالنسبة إلى time \( t \):
\[ a(t) = v'(t) = \frac{d}{dt}(6t^2 - 18t + 12) = 12t - 18. \]

Set \( a(t) = 0 \) and أوجد قيمة \( t \):
\[ 12t - 18 = 0 \implies 12t = 18 \implies t = \frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}. \]

Common Misconceptions:
- Solving \( v(t) = 0 \) yields \( 6(t - 1)(t - 2) = 0 \implies t = 1 \) or \( t = 2 \). These are the times عندما the particle is at rest, not عندما its acceleration is zero.
- Omitting the حلّل of 2 عندما applying the power rule gives \( 6t - 18 = 0 \implies t = 3 \).
